column2: PUBLIC BRANCH REGISTRY — every branch published on the remote, and what it is.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Corrections land on `main`. They do NOT land on feature branches,
which are frozen at the commit where work stopped. On 2026-08-08 all five non-main public
branches were found to carry a sentence retracted on main by CX-30 — a figure wrong by
~29 orders of magnitude, in the direction that flatters the project — and none of them
contains `documentation/CORRECTIONS.md` at all, because that file postdates them. A reader
who opens a branch therefore sees a withdrawn claim with no way to learn it was withdrawn.
No gate could see this: `doc_gates.sh` reads the working tree, and its one use of
`origin/main` is a COMMIT RANGE (origin/main..HEAD), never another branch's CONTENT.
GATE 19 closes that hole by enforcing THIS file — every published branch must be declared.
The declaration is the fix. Backporting 35 corrections into unmaintained feature branches
is the wrong shape of work, and one of these branches is pinned by a live campaign, so
rewriting it would put running compute at risk to correct prose.
status: authoritative | snapshot | merged | retired
authoritative — the published corpus. Corrections land here. Cite this.
snapshot      — frozen working branch. MAY CONTAIN CLAIMS SINCE CORRECTED ON MAIN.
Not a publication. Do not cite.
merged        — its tip is an ANCESTOR of main, so main already carries its content and
the branch is redundant. Declared here because this file records what is
PUBLISHED, not what is unmerged: the ref still exists on the remote and a
reader can still open it. The row retires when the ref is deleted, and
deletion is gated on tag-before-delete.
retired       — the ref is DELETED from the remote. The row stays because this file is how a
reader learns where the work went: column 4 names the tag that still pins the
exact commit, so `git branch <name> <tag>` restores it byte-for-byte. A row
removed instead of retired would leave a reader who has a citation to that
branch with nothing at all.
